rows.description: You're a punchline, a cautionary tale, or actively Blood Hunted. Kindred avoid associating with you for their own safety.
Dismissed and disrespected. Other Coteries openly poach from your territory and talk over you at gatherings.
Known, but not taken seriously. You get tolerant nods at Elysium and nothing else.
You exist on the radar. Nobody goes out of their way to help or hinder you. Sometimes they say "Hey."
Respected enough to get a seat at the table. Your name carries some weight in local politics.
A serious player. The Prince (or similar) knows your Coterie by name and considers you worth courting or watching.
Power brokers. Other Coteries actively seek your favor. Your endorsement or opposition shapes local Kindred politics.
Actively fractured. Members are scheming against each other. The Coterie exists in name only; it could dissolve any night.
Deep mistrust. Members withhold information, watch their backs, and have contingency plans for betrayal.
Strained. Old grudges or unresolved Debts make cooperation feel like pulling fangs.
Functional. You work together when you have to. Nobody's planning a betrayal, but nobody's taking a bullet for you either.
Solid. You trust each other enough to split up, share resources, and have honest disagreements without everything fracturing.
Tight-knit. Shared history, inside jokes, genuine loyalty. Members make sacrifices for each other without being asked.
Unbreakable bond. You'd walk into fire for each other (metaphorically; actual fire is still pretty scary, actually). Immune to the haters but not the sun.
Actively reviled. Mortals cross the street. Kindred assume the worst. Doors close before you even think about knocking.
Unpleasant reputation. People deal with you because they have to, not because they want to.
Offputting. First impressions go poorly. You have to work harder than most to earn basic goodwill.
Neutral. People form opinions based on direct interaction, not your reputation. You receive nods of acknowledgment sometimes.
Likable. People give you the benefit of the doubt. Strangers are inclined to help before they have a reason not to.
Magnetic. Your Coterie gets invited to things, remembered fondly, and forgiven for minor transgressions.
Beloved or fascinating. People (living and unliving) actively seek your company and make excuses for your behavior.
You're squatting somewhere that isn't yours and everyone knows it. Rivals are actively moving to take even that.
You have a room or a corner of a building, but it's contested. Someone else considers it theirs. They might be raccoons.
You have a place, but it's cramped, exposed, or in a location nobody else wanted. Rivals sniff around regularly.
A modest, defensible space. A house, a floor of a building, a warehouse. Unremarkable but functional.
A comfortable property with some breathing room. Neighbors and rival Kindred know it's yours.
A significant chunk of real estate; a block, a building complex, a stretch of waterfront. Other Kindred respect the boundary.
A whole neighborhood or borough answers to your Coterie. You are a landmark on the local Kindred political map.
You owe dangerous people real money. The kind of debt that gets kneecaps rearranged, mortal or otherwise.
Broke and in the hole. Can't cover emergencies. Pawning or stealing things to keep the lights on. Off is fine too, actually.
Scraping by. You can eat (figuratively) but a single unexpected expense is a crisis. Sound familiar?
Stable. Bills get paid, gear gets maintained, nobody's starving. No luxuries. Not even overnight shipping.
Comfortable. You can bribe a bouncer, replace a burned safehouse, or buy a decent used car without sweating.
Flush. Lawyers on retainer, slush funds, a vehicle or two, equipment upgrades when you need them.
Loaded. Shell companies, investment portfolios, properties plural. Money is a tool you wield, not a thing you worry about.
